extracted.intended_audience: USPTO-registered patent practitioners, attorneys/agents, OED staff, and legal professionals concerned with practitioner discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures for imposing reciprocal discipline (exclusion) by the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 when a practitioner has been publicly disciplined by a State. Includes procedural notice/response rules, scope of exclusion, publication and notification requirements, and ancillary technical/account actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by a State's highest court when a practitioner has been disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office files a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline and issues a Notice and Order to the respondent. The Notice and Order identifies the state discipline and requests imposition of identical discipline by the USPTO. See procedural steps (mailing, delivery, response period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional misconduct: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the USPTO rules, it is professional misconduct for a practitioner to be publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by any duly constituted authority of a State (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state public discipline for ethics/professional conduct is itself a basis for USPTO discipline; the Final Order cites this regulation as the basis for exclusion in reciprocal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and response procedure (40-day response period)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order must be mailed to the respondent (certified mail in this case) and the respondent is provided an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline based on the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery date starts the response period (Notice delivered April 8, 2013 in this case). The respondent may oppose on one or more statutory reasons; failure to file within the period is material to the outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond (default/no genuine issue finding)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a timely response, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and find reciprocal discipline appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order determined that, in light of Respondent's failure to file a response, exclusion was appropriate. Lack of a response supports entry of the requested reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of exclusion ordered
rubrics_metrics.description: The order may exclude the respondent from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO effective the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exclusion is imposed identical to the state discipline as provided by the reciprocal-discipline proceeding; the Final Order explicitly lists patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish a Notice in the Official Gazette announcing the respondent's exclusion and summarizing the reasons for the discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice should identify the respondent by name and registration number, state the basis for discipline (e.g., violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) by being disbarred in a particular State), summarize the state court's findings (e.g., commingling and conversion of client funds, violated specific Rules of Professional Conduct), cite statutory/regulatory authority (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24), and may provide a link to OED reading-room materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an affirmative obligation following imposition of discipline to ensure other jurisdictions and courts are informed of the USPTO action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and from any public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative/technical steps must be taken to remove the respondent's association with USPTO electronic access and filing credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on applying for or being added to USPTO Customer Number until reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Following exclusion, the respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction prevents excluded practitioners from using USPTO electronic filing or appearing in matters before reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underlying misconduct types that support reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of state-law misconduct that triggered reciprocal discipline in this case include commingling a client's funds (including unearned fees and filing fees) with personal account funds and converting those funds for personal use in violation of state Rules of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites Kansas Rules of Professional Conduct 1.15 (safekeeping property) and 8.4(c) (engaging in conduct involving misrepresentation) as the basis for the state disbarment; such ethical violations are the factual predicates for reciprocal USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The action is taken pursuant to federal statutory and regulatory authority, expressly 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing the statutory/regulatory bases is required in the Final Order to establish the USPTO's authority to impose the reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation of proceedings under new rules (37 C.F.R. § 11.901(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary proceedings initiated prior to the effective date of newly promulgated disciplinary rules may be continued under the new rules if the conduct at issue would continue to justify disciplinary action under the new rules (per 37 C.F.R. § 11.901(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order notes that although new disciplinary rules became effective May 3, 2013, reciprocal discipline against the respondent was unaffected because the conduct still constitutes professional misconduct under the new rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation basis when state discipline occurs (historic rule reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Historically, disciplinary proceedings were initiated under 37 C.F.R. § 10.23 (including subsections (a), (b), and (c)(5)) when a practitioner was disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order's footnote explains the agency's practice of initiating proceedings under the prior disciplinary rules and notes continuity of enforcement despite rule changes.
